---

## The Core Claim

In E. coli, genes for lactose metabolism (the lac operon) are switched on and off by a repressor protein that binds an operator DNA sequence, blocking transcription by default; when lactose (via allolactose) binds the repressor, it releases the operator, permitting transcription -- a real molecular feedback-control circuit, formally identical to negative feedback in control engineering (a sensor, a controlled variable, a de-repression switch), not a metaphor for one. Jacob, Monod, and Lwoff won the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering this genetic control mechanism.
